A '''cluster missile''' was one of a group of low-powered, unguided [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missiles]] that would rapidly fire in the direction that the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] which carried them was pointing. If a ship changed course while firing the missiles, the missiles that had not been fired yet would change their direction also, instead of seeking out the previous target.

Cluster missiles were used by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] in [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Starfighter combat/Legends|combat]],<ref name="FFGcard" /> and later equipped on [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[V-wing airspeeder]]s at the [[Battle of Calamari|Battle]] of [[Dac/Legends|Dac]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="RS I" />

Additionally, an [[Advanced cluster missile|upgraded]], [[Homing cluster missile|target-seeking]] variation of cluster missile was available.<ref name="RS I guide" /> Rather than firing in a standard formation, each of the six missiles could seek an individual target, or strike as a unified assault against a single ship.

But with [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|Darth Vader's TIE Advanced x1]], it shoots a cylindrical cluster of five missiles.

==Behind the scenes==
Cluster missiles first appeared in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]]s in [[1998]] with the release of [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]. Players may upgrade the cluster missiles to the seeker version by finding the upgrade in the [[Attack on Thyferra|Battle of Thyferra]] mission. In the game's sequel, [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader|''Rogue Leader'']], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] is equipped with cluster missiles during the bonus missions. That version is further upgradeable to the advanced version. In ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', the unlockable [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]] is equipped to carry cluster missiles. The ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Miniatures Game]]'' also features cluster missiles for simulated combat between Imperial and Rebel starfighters in [[Rebellion era]] combat.<ref name="FFGcard" />
